solutionNarrative: I first treated the set like a jungle or rainforest category because Vines, Orangutans, and Hammocks all live comfortably in that picture. That was plausible, but it stayed too broad and never explained why the board wanted five clues instead of one scene.

The turn came when I read Old tires as tire swing instead of junk hanging around a yard. Once swing became the shared action, the rest of the board tightened immediately: vines swing, orangutans swing, hammocks swing, and Tarzan is the most obvious swinging image of all.

lessons.title: Do not stop at the setting if the action is stronger
lessons.body: A board can look like it is describing one place, but the better answer is often the action that ties every clue together.

lessons.body: Once swing showed up as the real connector, each clue could be tested quickly against the same action instead of a vague category.
